doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents' origins and the seven Young children
summary: Young gives his father's Dayton roots, his mother's Virginia roots, and names his brothers and sisters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Where was your father from? Where did your father come, what was his hometown?
My father‘s hometown was Dayton, Ohio
Ok, so he was born and raised in Dayton?
He was born and raised in Dayton.
And your mother‘s name and where was she from?

My mother was from Virginia. I don‘t remember the name of the city or anything, but I know she was from Virginia. Her family moved to Ohio, I can‘t tell you too much about that because it was before I was born. So I do know that my mother was from Virginia.
Ok, ok. Do you have, did you have, or do you have any brothers or sisters?

Yes, I have. There was seven of us in my family, four boys and three girls. My oldest brother was Granville, Granville Young. I was the second, no I wasn‘t second, my sister was second, Mary-Louise, and then I was third; Eugene Edward Young. The fourth child was, was it Ursabelle? I think it was Ursabelle. It‘s hard for me to remember of my sisters and brothers now it‘s been so many years. Ursabelle and then Jimmy; James Young. And then my youngest brother was Don Young. I think that was all seven of my sisters and brothers.
Judy, go ahead, you can make an addendum. Judy Andrews: Joanne…
Thank you. Joanne was my youngest sister, that was the last child that made us seven, I missed…
